That position is hazardous nationally: no department criminalises anything about being trans and gender-identity recognition is administered nationally, while monitoring bodies recorded 270 LGBTIQ+ killings in 2025 (one every 32 hours, a 63% increase on 2024's 164), and the reporting shows lethal anti-trans violence can occur in daylight with the perpetrator unarrested.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: The incidents the sources document unfolded in other departments: the transfeminicide in Bello, Antioquia (April 2025) — an attack at which onlookers filmed and which went viral, with no one arrested even after the president ordered an urgent investigation — and the armed-group 'social cleansing' campaign in Caquetá, another department (July 2024), in which flyers on the streets and warning messages on phones named categories of people as legitimate military targets and a trans woman was given one week to leave town. The country's monitoring bodies describe anti-LGBTIQ violence expanding territorially into departments where the state response is weakest.
